idea-plugin.name: VerifyLens
idea-plugin.description:
See per requirement whether an AI-generated change is verified, different, or not yet verified, before you commit.

AI tools say "Done, all requirements implemented." VerifyLens checks that claim against your working tree and the tests that actually ran, and shows the result in a tool window and next to the code line that decides each requirement, for example ← R2 · Different · acts on attempt 6 (requirement: 5) · but the test passes.

The tests can all pass and the requirement can still be unmet: when the AI writes the code and the test with the same misunderstanding. VerifyLens computes when a numeric condition fires, so it catches that case too.

  • No LLM, and your code never leaves your machine. Static analysis + git + your JUnit test results, all local. No telemetry.
  • Unknown stays unknown. No test or an unresolved call means "not verified", never "looks fine".
  • The evidence chain as a picture. requirement → code line → tests → when it acts, drawn in the tool window. A missing link is a grey dashed box, so you can see why a requirement is not verified.
  • Tests changed to pass are shown. When a linked test was edited or removed in the same change, the requirement is marked "test changed".
  • Same engine as the VS Code extension, so both editors give the same verdict.

Preview. Analyzes TypeScript and JavaScript. Needs Node.js 18+ and git on this machine. The UI is in English or Korean and follows the IDE language (Tools | VerifyLens | Language… changes it).

AI가 「완료」라고 한 변경이 요구사항마다 확인됨 · 다름 · 미확인인지, 커밋하기 전에 에디터에서 보여 줍니다. AI 판정 없이 코드 분석과 실제로 돌린 테스트 결과만 쓰고, 코드는 PC 밖으로 나가지 않습니다.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.15.0: follows the engine of VS Code 0.21.0, and fixes projects opened through a link. For a requirement that blocks something ("a locked account cannot log in"), a block that only sets the state is not the check for it: the evidence is the line that tests the state (if (user.locked) …), not the block that sets it, and a single assignment is not evidence. This removes cases that were Verified with no check. Projects opened through a mapped drive (subst V:), a junction or a symbolic link: the tool window showed the result, but the editor had no line-end note and no gutter icon, and saving a file did not check again. git reports the repository by its real path; the plugin now keeps the path the IDE opened.

0.14.0: follows the engine of VS Code 0.20.0. Korean keywords are read: "| keywords: 실패, 잠금" is linked to failures and locked in the code through the glossary that already links Korean sentences. Before, almost every requirement with Korean keywords was Not verified. The one-line summary agrees with the evidence row: when a linked test passes but something else keeps the requirement Not verified, it names that reason ("the test passes, but no deciding check") instead of "no linked test". On an English screen, Korean units are shown in English ("allows up to 3 times", "50,000 won"). Verdicts change only for requirements with Korean keywords.

0.13.0: the evidence chain is drawn in the tool window. Under the list, the selected requirement is shown as four boxes, requirement → code line → tests → when it acts, from the same model and in the same colours as the report and the try-it page. A missing link is a grey dashed box, so a Not verified requirement shows which link is missing. When the attempt can be computed, a row of dots shows the required attempt and the one the code acts on (Required 5, Code 6, "1 late"). Click the code box to go to the line, or the tests box to go to a test that was changed in this change. The verdict colours in the list, the gutter and the line background now match the report. The engine and the verdicts are the same as in 0.12.0.

0.12.0: follows the engine of VS Code 0.19.0 and shows tests that were changed in this change. When a test linked to a requirement was edited, removed or skipped in the same change (a loop of 5 became 6, an expected value was replaced), the requirement keeps its verdict and gets "⚠ test changed" next to it, with a row under it that names the test and what changed (test/auth.test.ts:5 — test changed in this change: 5 → 6). Click the row to open the test. The verdicts are the same as in 0.11.0.

0.11.0: follows the engine of VS Code 0.17.0 and 0.18.0. A check in another feature's function is not evidence, even in a file named for the requirement (in signup.ts, the email check in subscribe no longer verifies "sign-up rejects an invalid email"). A check on another state or role is not evidence ("orders that have started shipping cannot be cancelled" with code that blocks only 'delivered'). class-validator decorators (@IsEmail(), @IsUUID(), @Length(2, 50), @Min / @Max) are read as checks. "At most 3 per day" needs a time window: a count with no time filter is Not verified with the reason "no time window". A count kept in a variable is read like list.length. "Only once" needs a check that looks at whether it was already used. A reminder "3 days before" means that day. "~할 수 없다" is read as a rejection rule.

0.10.0: a fixed amount computed as a percentage is Different: in a branch for fixed, flat or amount, total * (1 - v / 100) is reported as "computes the fixed amount as a percentage", even when a test passes. A format check in a schema (z.string().uuid(), .email(), .url(), yup and Joi) is evidence, and regex(/^\d{11}$/) is read as exactly 11 characters. A check in a function for another action is not evidence (the id check in getFile does not verify deleteFile). if (prev) return prev counts as a duplicate check. With keywords, a rejection rule links only tests that say reject.

0.9.0: a check in a function for another feature is no longer evidence (a newsletter's email check does not verify "sign-up rejects an invalid email"). A schema field taken without a check (email: z.string()) keeps a rejection rule unverified and shows the line. "Only once" needs a test that does it twice. "Even if pressed twice" is read as a scene, not a limit of two. Coupon amounts (FLAT_COUPON = 5000) are read as settings.

0.8.0: a line that only shares a number or a unit with the requirement (a string length, a list length, LOCK_MINUTES in another file, a sign-up form's age) is no longer used as evidence. A fraction is no longer within one of a whole percent (0.02 was Verified against 1%). Counting first and then rejecting allows the limit. "Once every 30 days" means 30 days must pass. Settings with a generic name (maxAge) are linked through the statement that sets them.

0.7.0: reads "are not accepted" as a refusal, "once per person" as a uniqueness check, rates stored as fractions (0.1 = 10%) and timer values (setInterval). A setting named for another thing (RETURN_FEE for a shipping fee) is no longer used as evidence.

0.6.0: time rules are read better: a time difference with no name (Date.now() - sentAt), "14 days after", "1 hour before", "1 minute window", and "blocked when it is 0".

0.5.0: says why a requirement is unverified (wording, edge value, execution order, no deciding check, no test …) and what to do next. Sign-up rules are read better: a required check must exist, "only once" is not a count, "6 digits" means exactly 6. A second setting with the same name and another value keeps the result unverified.

0.4.1: first version for JetBrains Marketplace. Adds the plugin icon. The analysis is the same as 0.4.0.

0.4.0: reads range wording such as "up to and including", "must not exceed", "3 to 20" and "1~10", and judges more requirements without keywords.

action.description: Checks each requirement against your working tree (uncommitted changes included) and the base branch
Shows VerifyLens on a login-lockout example, without touching your code
Creates .verifylens/requirements.md with two example lines and opens it
Chooses the Node.js executable that runs the analysis engine
